title: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning of Small Transformers for Text Classification
raw_text: We study parameter-efficient fine-tuning of small transformer models (under 200M parameters) for text classification. LoRA adapters keep the base model frozen, cutting optimizer state and memory to a few hundred megabytes. Training a classification head plus adapters for three epochs completes in under two hours on a mid-range laptop CPU. We report accuracy within 1.5 points of full fine-tuning while using an order of magnitude less memory.

title: cpu-vector-search: HNSW-style search that never touches a GPU
raw_text: A from-scratch vector search library that runs entirely on CPU. Implements an HNSW-style graph index with 128-dim float32 embeddings, brute-force and approximate search, and single-threaded and parallel query paths. A 1M-vector index fits in about 200MB of RAM. No GPU code anywhere; benchmarks compare against faiss-cpu only.

title: Training a 70B-Parameter Dense LLM from Scratch on Two Trillion Tokens
raw_text: We train a 70-billion-parameter dense decoder-only model from scratch on two trillion tokens using a cluster of 1024 A100 GPUs for six months. Pipeline parallelism, ZeRO-3 sharding, and tensor-parallel embeddings are required throughout. Total compute is roughly 2.5e25 FLOPs. Loss curves show no saturation, suggesting additional scale would help.

title: Scaling Text-to-Image Diffusion to Five Billion Image-Text Pairs
raw_text: We propose a large-scale text-to-image diffusion model trained on five billion image-text pairs across eight A100 GPUs per node. Inference requires over 40GB of VRAM in fp16 and uses classifier-free guidance with a 3B-parameter UNet and a frozen CLIP text encoder. Distillation to a smaller student model is left as future work.

title: A Compact Retrieval-Augmented Generation Pipeline for CPU-Only Machines
raw_text: We build a retrieval-augmented generation pipeline using a 33M-parameter embedding model and a 1.5B-parameter reader, both running in fp16 on an 8GB CPU-only machine. An index of ten thousand documents fits entirely in memory. End-to-end latency stays under four seconds per query, and memory peaks at roughly 5.5GB. A streaming mode trades a little accuracy for faster first tokens.

title: Show HN: Real-time 4x video super-resolution with RIFE-style optical flow
raw_text: Real-time 4x video super-resolution at 60fps using an RIFE-style optical flow model. Requires an RTX 3090 for realtime throughput; the CPU fallback runs at roughly 2fps on an eight-core machine. Model weights are 200MB and the flow estimation stage alone uses 11GB of GPU memory.

title: struct-extract: dependency-free CLI for extracting records from messy text
raw_text: A dependency-free Python CLI that extracts structured records (dates, names, amounts) from messy text using regex rules plus a small scoring pass to resolve conflicts. Pure standard library, no LLM required. Processes 100k documents in a few minutes on a single core with peak memory under 300MB. Ships a YAML rule file so users can add custom record types.

title: Pretraining a Vision Transformer from Scratch on ImageNet-1K
raw_text: We pretrain an 86M-parameter Vision Transformer on ImageNet-1K from scratch using eight NVIDIA V100 GPUs for 90 epochs with a batch size of 4096 and gradient accumulation. Mixed-precision training is mandatory to fit the optimizer state. Distillation to a CPU-friendly student is mentioned only as a downstream idea.

title: pure-md: a spec-compliant CommonMark parser in pure Python
raw_text: A spec-compliant CommonMark markdown parser written in pure Python with zero dependencies. A tokenizer and AST builder run in linear time, tested against over 600 spec cases, and used in production for static site generation. Includes an HTML renderer and a JSON AST serializer. Memory use stays well under 50MB even for very long documents.

title: A Novel Approach to Protein Structure Prediction with MSA on HPC
raw_text: We present a novel approach to protein structure prediction that requires roughly 5000 GPU-hours per target and 128GB of RAM for the multiple sequence alignment stage. A single fold takes two to three days on an HPC cluster with 64 cores and four A100s. The paper focuses on accuracy gains over baselines rather than efficiency.

title: Two-Pass Summarization of 100k-Token Documents on an 8GB Laptop
raw_text: We compress 100k-token documents into structured summaries using a two-pass extractive-then-abstractive pipeline. Pass one runs a CPU-friendly BM25-based sentence scorer over the whole document; pass two feeds only the top-ranked sentences to a 1B-parameter generative model. Peak memory is 6GB and runtime is about three minutes per document on an eight-core laptop. The scorer is a hundred lines of plain Python with no external dependencies.

title: tiny-asr: streaming speech-to-text with a 39M-parameter Whisper variant
raw_text: Real-time speech-to-text on a Raspberry-Pi-class device using a distilled 39M-parameter Whisper variant. Streaming chunking with a voice activity detector, greedy decoding, and a word error rate within eight points of the large models. Peak memory is 1.2GB, and the model runs in pure fp32 on a quad-core ARM CPU with no GPU or accelerator.
